messages:
Ivy (People Ops): quick policy check  Casey is moving from 1.0 -> 0.6 FTE on 04/15. They already booked the company bridge day on 04/18 (was full-time eligible). Manager asks whether we should pro-rate or convert the bridge day into PTO hours. Also question on accrual cap for part-timers mid-year.

Dee (Engineering): Casey asked to keep the bridge day because they planned travel. worried about changing plans last minute. manager said might be OK if we credit equivalent hours.

Ramon (Manager): i prefer to convert rather than force a reschedule. Can we give pro-rated hours so they don't lose value? Also confirm whether this impacts their year-end carryover cap.

PeopleOps Bot: policy note: Bridge days are company-designated paid days off for full-time employees. For FTE changes mid-year, common practice: (a) pro-rate bridge day to hourly equivalent and credit to PTO if crossing to PT before the bridge date; (b) document as RECLASS_BRIDGE exception. Carryover cap still applies based on employee's FTE at year-end; exceptions require manager + People Ops approval. See: https://redwood.example/hr/bridge-days

Ivy (People Ops): Proposed approach:
1) If FTE change effective before bridge date (04/15 < 04/18) convert bridge day to PTO hours: 8 * 0.6 = 4.8 hours (round to nearest 0.25 hr -> 4.75).
2) Create EXC-2027-701 stating rounding rule and manager approval.
3) If carryover bump needed (they'd hit accrual cap), manager must sign off and we file a CAP_EXCEPTION.
Would you like us to proceed with the credit?

Ramon (Manager): yes please proceed. i approve converting bridge day to PTO hours for Casey M. and applying standard rounding. if carryover cap hits, approve one-time cap exception so they don't lose it.

Dee (Engineering): thx. can you also confirm whether payroll needs an adjustment for FTE change affecting accruals?

Samir (Payroll): payroll note: accrual rates change with FTE; for mid-pay-period changes we typically prorate accruals from change date forward and do a one-time balance update for the bridge conversion. Tax impact is nil for PTO hours transfer. We'll need the EXC id to attach to payroll ticket.

Jasper L.: From HRIS side I can run the update. Steps I'll take:
- Create EXC-2027-701 in exceptions system.
- Run hrcli adjust-balance --user casey.m --add 4.75 --type PTO --note "Bridge day reclass (EXC-2027-701) due to FTE change"
- Adjust accrual schedule effective 04/15 to 0.6 FTE.
Let me know when you want me to run it.

Ivy (People Ops): I'll file EXC-2027-701 now and queue the HRIS update for 04/15 end-of-day. Ramon please confirm one more time (single-line) that you approve the cap exception if rounding pushes Casey over carryover limits.

Ramon (Manager): approve cap exception if needed so Casey doesn't lose time.

Ivy (People Ops): thanks  filing EXC-2027-701 and creating payroll ticket PL-10333. Jasper, please execute the hrcli command on 2027-04-15 EOD and attach EXC-2027-701 and payroll ticket.

PeopleOps Bot: Actions created: EXC-2027-701, PL-10333. Reminder: document employee consent for FTE change in file. Link: https://redwood.example/hr/exceptions/EXC-2027-701

Samir (Payroll): got it  i'll review accrual proration and confirm no tax impact.

Ivy (People Ops): closing loop once HRIS update completes. TL;DR: allowed to convert bridge day to pro-rated PTO for mid-year FTE reductions, require manager sign-off + exception record + payroll coordination. Prefer swaps if it avoids accrual churn. :white_check_mark:
